header_evidence.locator: SS1-SRC-470d43e54e5b: third line of mammoth 1.12.2 extractRawText() output (the importer's own .docx call), after the title line 'LIT-IN-ENGLISH'; trailing whitespace of the line is not included
header_evidence.explanation: The document opens with the title 'LIT-IN-ENGLISH' (occurs once) and then this scheme heading, which occurs once and names Literature-in-English and class SS1; the document has no 'SUBJECT:' line. The subject is verified by the document and not by the filename, and it is not English Language: the scheme lists introduction to the study of literature, genres (drama, prose, poetry), fiction and non-fiction, elements of prose, features and forms of poetry, drama, oral literature, and Week 1 teaching separates English Literature from Literature-In-English. The heading differs from the canonical name by the 'SCHEME OF WORK FOR' prefix and class label, so a source_alias is declared.

header_evidence.explanation: The subject line occurs once in the extracted text ('LITERATURE' alone occurs 4 times). It names Literature-in-English, and lines 1 and 3 name the second term and class SS1, so subject and term are verified by the document and not by the filename. The scheme lists African drama (Harvest of Corruption, The Blood of a Stranger), African poetry (Piano and Drums) and further set texts, and Week One teaches Harvest of Corruption, so it is not English Language. The heading differs from the canonical name 'Literature-in-English' (used by LIT-SRC-T1) by spaces and en dashes, so a source_alias is declared. The title line carries a session year, 2016/2017, which is not used as evidence of the term.

header_evidence.explanation: The subject line occurs once in the extracted text ('LITERATURE' alone occurs 4 times case-insensitively, 1 time in upper case). It names Literature-in-English, and lines 1 and 3 name the third term and class SS1, so subject and term are verified by the document and not by the filename. The scheme lists African drama (Harvest of Corruption, The Blood of a Stranger), African poetry (Piano and Drums, The Dining Table, The Anvil and the Hammer) and non-African drama (Othello, She Stoops to Conquer), and Week One teaches Harvest of Corruption, so it is not English Language. The heading differs from the canonical name 'Literature-in-English' (used by LIT-SRC-T1) by spaces and en dashes, so a source_alias is declared. Unlike the 2nd Term title, this title line carries no session year.
